tools.name: send_email
tools.rationale: `send_email` sends agent-supplied `subject`, `body`, optional `attachments`, `cc`, and `bcc` to agent-chosen `recipients` via `Inbox.send_email`, so it is a SINK. The returned `Email` includes `sender=self.account_email`, exposing account data from the inbox.

tools.name: delete_email
tools.rationale: `delete_email` changes inbox state by removing the selected email and placing it in trash, but the advertised wrapper returns only a fixed success string and does not send data to an outside destination.

tools.name: get_unread_emails
tools.rationale: Returns unread emails from the user's inbox, which are non-public account data. Received email `sender`, `subject`, `body`, and attachments can be authored by outside senders. It also marks emails read, so it is WRITE.

tools.name: get_sent_emails
tools.rationale: Returns sent emails stored in the user's inbox account, which are non-public account data.

tools.name: get_received_emails
tools.rationale: Returns received emails from the user's inbox account. Received messages are non-public to the account and their `sender`, `subject`, `body`, and attachments can be authored by outside senders.

tools.name: get_draft_emails
tools.rationale: Returns draft emails stored in the user's inbox account, which are non-public account data.

tools.name: search_emails
tools.rationale: Searches emails in the user's inbox account and returns matching `Email` records. Because the search can return received emails, returned `sender`, `subject`, `body`, and attachments may be attacker-authored.

tools.name: search_contacts_by_name
tools.rationale: Searches the user's inbox-derived contact list. Contacts are built from email senders/recipients, so an outside sender can introduce attacker-controlled email/name values into returned contacts.

tools.name: search_contacts_by_email
tools.rationale: Searches the user's inbox-derived contact list. Contacts are built from email senders/recipients, so an outside sender can introduce attacker-controlled email/name values into returned contacts.

tools.name: get_current_day
tools.rationale: Returns only the calendar's current date string and does not read event content, change state, or send data to an outside destination.

tools.name: search_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Searches and returns calendar events stored in the user's calendar account. Event `title`, `description`, `location`, and participant data can come from events/invitations authored by other parties.

tools.name: get_day_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Returns calendar events for a day from the user's calendar account. Event `title`, `description`, `location`, and participant data can come from events/invitations authored by other parties.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Creates a calendar event and sends an invitation email with agent-supplied event details to agent-chosen `participants`, so it is a SINK. The returned event includes calendar account data such as the owner email added to `participants`.

tools.name: cancel_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Cancels the selected event and sends a cancellation email with the event attached to that event's participants. The `event_id` selects the record changed and the participant destination set used by the send.

tools.name: reschedule_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Reschedules the selected event and sends an email with the new time to the event's participants, so it can deliver agent-supplied time data outward. It returns the calendar event, which is non-public account data and may contain externally authored event fields.

tools.name: add_calendar_event_participants
tools.rationale: Modifies a calendar event's participants and returns the event. The returned event is non-public calendar data and may contain externally authored event fields. The code does not actually send the email mentioned in the description.

tools.name: append_to_file
tools.rationale: Appends agent-supplied content to a selected cloud-drive file and returns the full file. Cloud-drive file content is non-public account data and may include shared or third-party-authored file content.

tools.name: search_files_by_filename
tools.rationale: Returns matching cloud-drive files including contents from the user's account. Files may be shared/downloaded documents authored by outside parties, making file names/content potentially attacker-controlled.

tools.name: create_file
tools.rationale: Creates a new file in the user's cloud drive and returns it. The returned object includes account data such as `owner=self.account_email`. It does not send data to an outside destination.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.rationale: Deletes a selected cloud-drive file and returns the deleted file including its content. That file is non-public account data and may be a shared/downloaded attacker-authored document.

tools.name: get_file_by_id
tools.rationale: Returns a cloud-drive file by ID including content from the user's account. The file may be a shared/downloaded attacker-authored document.

tools.name: list_files
tools.rationale: Returns all cloud-drive files in the user's account, including file contents. Some files may be shared/downloaded attacker-authored documents.

tools.name: share_file
tools.rationale: Grants an agent-chosen `email` access to a selected file by writing `file.shared_with[email] = permission`, so it can expose file data to an attacker-readable recipient. It returns the file, whose content is non-public account data and may be externally authored.

tools.name: search_files
tools.rationale: Searches cloud-drive file contents and returns matching files from the user's account. Returned file names/content may be attacker-authored shared or downloaded documents.

tools.name: get_channels
tools.rationale: Returns the Slack workspace channel list via `return slack.channels`; Slack workspace data is non-public account/workspace data.

tools.name: add_user_to_channel
tools.rationale: Mutates Slack membership by validating an existing `user` and `channel` and appending the channel to `slack.user_channels[user]`. It returns no data and does not send message content in the code shown.

tools.name: read_channel_messages
tools.rationale: Returns messages from `slack.channel_inbox` for the selected channel. Channel messages are non-public Slack workspace data, and in a multi-writer Slack channel outside users can author message `body` and identify themselves as `sender`.

tools.name: read_inbox
tools.rationale: Returns messages from `slack.user_inbox` for the selected user. Inbox messages are non-public Slack data, and messages received from other users can contain attacker-authored `body` text and attacker-named `sender` values.

tools.name: send_direct_message
tools.rationale: Creates a `Message` with agent-supplied `body` and appends it to an agent-chosen `recipient`'s Slack inbox, so it can deliver data to an agent-chosen Slack user.

tools.name: send_channel_message
tools.rationale: Creates a `Message` with agent-supplied `body` and appends it to an agent-chosen Slack `channel`, so it can deliver data to channel readers, including attacker-readable channels if chosen.

tools.name: get_users_in_channel
tools.rationale: Reads `slack.user_channels` membership and returns the users in the selected Slack channel; channel membership is non-public workspace data.

tools.name: invite_user_to_slack
tools.rationale: The tool is an invite operation and its docstring says `user_email` is where the invite should be sent. The implementation shown only appends the new `user` to Slack state and initializes inbox/channel state, so actual outbound delivery to `user_email` is not shown; the SINK label is raised by the invite/email behavior described in the tool text.

tools.name: remove_user_from_slack
tools.rationale: Deletes the selected `user` from Slack state and associated inbox/channel mappings. It returns no data and does not send agent-supplied content to another destination in the code shown.

tools.name: get_webpage
tools.rationale: Standardizes an agent-supplied `url`, records it in `web.web_requests`, and returns `web.web_content.get(url)`. Attacker-controlled web hosts can provide attacker-authored page text, so the return is UNTRUSTED. Because the URL is agent-chosen, the request can be made to an attacker-readable destination and can also target localhost/intranet/private URLs if present; the code shows no restriction, so SECRET reach is kept as undetermined.

tools.name: post_webpage
tools.rationale: Standardizes an agent-supplied `url`, records the request, and stores agent-supplied `content` in `web.web_content[url]`, allowing data to be posted to an agent-chosen web destination.

tools.name: get_user_information
tools.rationale: Returns private user profile and financial/identity fields from the `user` dependency, including ID, passport, bank account, and credit card numbers.

tools.name: get_all_hotels_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns hotel names from a travel listing dataset. The code does not establish provenance of `hotels.hotel_list`; under the threat model public/third-party registries can contain attacker-authored business names.

tools.name: get_hotels_prices
tools.rationale: Returns a mapping keyed by hotel names with price data from `hotels.hotel_list`. The code does not establish provenance of the travel registry data, so hotel names/prices are treated as third-party controlled.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_hotels
tools.rationale: Returns hotel names and joined `hotel.reviews`; reviews are third-party/public content and the code does not constrain their authorship.

tools.name: get_hotels_address
tools.rationale: Returns hotel names and addresses from `hotels.hotel_list`. The code does not establish provenance of the travel registry data, so these public listing fields are treated as attacker-controllable.

tools.name: get_all_restaurants_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names from a travel/restaurant listing dataset. The code does not establish provenance of `restaurants.restaurant_list`; public registry entries may be attacker-authored.

tools.name: get_cuisine_type_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names and cuisine types from `restaurants.restaurant_list`; provenance is not established in code, so public listing text is treated as attacker-controllable.

tools.name: get_restaurants_address
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names and addresses from `restaurants.restaurant_list`. The code does not establish provenance of these public listing fields.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names and joined `restaurant.reviews`; reviews are third-party/public content and the code does not constrain their authorship.

tools.name: get_dietary_restrictions_for_all_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names and dietary-restriction text from `restaurants.restaurant_list`; provenance is not established in code, so public listing text is treated as attacker-controllable.

tools.name: get_contact_information_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names and contact information from a public/third-party restaurant listing; the code does not establish provenance.

tools.name: get_price_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names and price data from `restaurants.restaurant_list`; the listing provenance is not established in code.

tools.name: check_restaurant_opening_hours
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant names and operating-hours text from a public/third-party listing; the code does not establish provenance.

tools.name: get_all_car_rental_companies_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental company names from a travel listing dataset. The code does not establish provenance of `car_rental.company_list`; public registry entries may be attacker-authored.

tools.name: get_car_types_available
tools.rationale: Returns company names and available car-type lists from `car_rental.company_list`; listing provenance is not established in code.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_car_rental
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental company names and joined `company.reviews`; reviews are third-party/public content and the code does not constrain their authorship.

tools.name: get_car_fuel_options
tools.rationale: Returns company names and fuel-option lists from `car_rental.company_list`; listing provenance is not established in code.

tools.name: get_car_rental_address
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental company names and addresses from a public/third-party listing; the code does not establish provenance.

tools.name: get_car_price_per_day
tools.rationale: Returns company names and price data from `car_rental.company_list`; listing provenance is not established in code.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Creates a calendar event in the user's calendar and returns it, including the calendar account email added to `participants`. It also sends an email to agent-supplied `participants` with the event details, making it a sink.

tools.name: search_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Searches and returns events from the user's calendar, which is non-public account data. The code does not establish event provenance; calendar events may include third-party invitations with attacker-authored titles/descriptions/locations/participants.

tools.name: get_day_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Returns events from the user's calendar for a day, which is non-public account data. The code does not establish event provenance; calendar events may include attacker-authored third-party invitation fields.

tools.name: cancel_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Marks the selected event canceled and sends an email with the event attached to that event's participants via `inbox.send_email`. The agent controls which event is selected via `event_id`, which determines the record changed and the notified participants.

tools.name: reserve_hotel
tools.rationale: Changes the local `reservation` dependency to a hotel reservation and stores the hotel name and dates. The code does not send the reservation to an external party or return private user data.

tools.name: reserve_car_rental
tools.rationale: Changes the local `reservation` dependency to a car-rental reservation and stores the company and times. The code does not send the reservation to an external party or return private user data.

tools.name: reserve_restaurant
tools.rationale: Changes the local `reservation` dependency to a restaurant reservation and stores the restaurant and time. The code does not send the reservation to an external party or return private user data.

tools.name: get_flight_information
tools.rationale: Returns flight and contact information from `flights.flight_list`. The code does not establish provenance of this travel information, so public/third-party listing text is treated as attacker-controllable.

tools.name: send_email
tools.rationale: Constructs and stores a sent email with agent-supplied `recipients`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `body`, and attachments. The destination email addresses are agent-chosen, so it can deliver data to attacker-readable recipients.

tools.name: get_iban
tools.rationale: `get_iban` returns `account.iban`, the user's current bank account identifier, from the private `bank_account` dependency.

tools.name: send_money
tools.rationale: `send_money` creates a `Transaction` addressed to the agent-supplied `recipient` with agent-supplied `amount`, `subject`, and `date`, then appends it to `account.transactions`; this models sending money to an agent-chosen bank account/recipient.

tools.name: schedule_transaction
tools.rationale: `schedule_transaction` creates a future `Transaction` for the agent-supplied `recipient` with supplied payment details and appends it to `account.scheduled_transactions`, scheduling a payment to an agent-chosen account.

tools.name: update_scheduled_transaction
tools.rationale: `update_scheduled_transaction` selects a scheduled payment by agent-supplied `id` and can change its `recipient`, `amount`, `subject`, `date`, and `recurring` fields, including redirecting or modifying a scheduled payment.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.rationale: `get_balance` returns `account.balance` from the user's private bank account dependency.

tools.name: get_most_recent_transactions
tools.rationale: `get_most_recent_transactions` returns entries from `account.transactions`, exposing private banking history. Returned `Transaction` objects include text fields such as `sender` and `subject`; for received transactions, the payer/outside party can author the sender identifier and transaction subject.

tools.name: get_scheduled_transactions
tools.rationale: `get_scheduled_transactions` returns `account.scheduled_transactions`, exposing the user's private scheduled banking transactions and their identifiers/account numbers.

tools.name: read_file
tools.rationale: `read_file` returns the contents of an arbitrary entry in the host-like `filesystem.files` mapping selected by `file_path`, so it can expose non-public files. File contents can include documents received from third parties, whose text is attacker-authored under the threat model.

tools.name: get_user_info
tools.rationale: `get_user_info` returns private user account profile data (`first_name`, `last_name`, `street`, and `city`) from the `user_account` dependency.

tools.name: update_password
tools.rationale: `update_password` writes the supplied `password` into the local `user_account` object and returns only a fixed confirmation message; it does not return secrets or send data to an attacker-readable destination in the code shown.

tools.name: update_user_info
tools.rationale: `update_user_info` mutates the private user account profile fields and returns the resulting `first_name`, `last_name`, `street`, and `city`; if some optional fields are omitted, existing non-public account data is returned.
